question: Do the passages support using larger language-model context windows as a complete substitute for retrieval when synthesizing many papers?
required_claim: Larger windows help capacity but do not replace careful retrieval; omitted retrieved evidence still breaks synthesis.

passages.text: A coffee shop near the lab introduced a student loyalty card.
Methods note J: Expanding the context window increases how much text can be pasted in, but models may still under-use middle passages when synthesizing many claims.
GPU fan noise complaints were logged in the shared compute room.
A packaging inventory listed spare Ethernet cables in Cabinet 4.
The department newsletter announced a guest talk on robotics.
Bike rack capacity near the library was expanded by twelve slots.
Methods note K: If a retriever fails to surface a required paper passage, the synthesizer cannot cite it—so retrieval quality remains a separate failure mode even with long context.
